yq: JSON flow-mapping token-pairing grammar (#2777) needs route unification for --inplace/--slurp/--eval-all

## Context

#2777 (fixed in this issue's own PR) adds real yq's token-pairing grammar for
JSON-sourced flow mappings (`-p json`'s `{...}`) on the "plain" route
(`YamlIndex`-backed parsing, used by ordinary evaluation without
`--inplace`/`--slurp`/`--eval-all`). Two things were deliberately scoped out
of that fix, both documented in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s
"Closed by #2777" section:

## 1. Route unification (DOM bridge still uses the old strict grammar)

`--inplace`/`--slurp`/`--eval-all` materialize JSON input through a separate
code path — `yq_runner::parse_input`'s `InputFormat::Json` arm, which uses
`JsonIndex` + `to_owned_canonicalizing_numbers_at_depth` rather than
`YamlIndex::build_json_sourced`. That route still applies #1975's own
stricter-than-real-yq JSON grammar, so it does not get #2777's leniency:

```console
$ printf '{"a":1 "b":2}' > /tmp/f.json
$ yq -p json -o json -I0 --inplace '.' /tmp/f.json && cat /tmp/f.json
{"a":1,"b":2}
$ succinctly yq -p json -o json -I0 --inplace '.' /tmp/f.json
Error: Invalid JSON text: expected ',' or '}', found '"'
```

Fixing this means making `yq_runner::parse_input`'s `InputFormat::Json` arm
build through `YamlIndex::build_json_sourced` too (instead of `JsonIndex`),
which would also require carrying `JsonIndex`'s own number-canonicalization
pass over to the YAML-cursor-backed walk. This is a separate, larger change
that touches the destructive `--inplace` write path, so it needs its own
careful test coverage (proving nothing is written on a rejected file, and
that `--inplace` now rewrites what real yq rewrites) rather than being
folded into #2777's own fix.

## 2. "Any bracket ends the loop" is not reproduced

Real yq's token scanner treats *every* bracket character (`{`, `}`, `[`,
`]`) as a `Delim` that ends the *current* object's key-reading loop the
instant one is seen — not just its own matching closing brace:

```console
$ printf '{"a":1 ]}' | yq -p json -o json -I0 '.'
{"a":1}
$ printf '{[1]:2}' | yq -p json -o json -I0 '.'
{}
```

Whatever is left unconsumed in that case is then read as the *next*
top-level document by yq's own stream evaluator, whose own trailing-content
handling is itself inconsistent (some leftover shapes produce no visible
error at all; others print a stream-decode error to stderr while still
emitting the correct value and exiting 0). Reproducing this faithfully would
mean modelling a second, top-level-only decoder loop with the same
inconsistency, for a shape (a bare bracket standing in for a key, with no
quotes at all) that essentially never occurs in real-world JSON.

succinctly currently reports an ordinary parse error for a `{`/`[`/`]` found
where a key is expected (always failing the whole document cleanly), rather
than silently producing a truncated one — a safe-direction divergence, never
a wrong value, just a narrower acceptance set than the reference's own
accidental leniency here.

## Suggested approach

- For (1): thread `YamlIndex::build_json_sourced` through
  `yq_runner::parse_input`'s JSON arm, replacing `JsonIndex`; verify
  `parse_input_m2_parity`'s depth pre-check still holds (the YAML parser
  already enforces `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` at parse time).
- For (2): lower priority given how rarely a bare bracket appears where a
  key is expected in real-world JSON; if tackled, needs its own model of
  yq's inconsistent trailing-content handling, which may be more trouble
  than it's worth to chase byte-for-byte.

Related: #2777, #1975, #2279, #2778, #2781, #2845.
